newsitem.title: USA: Wired IPO pricing on hold - Goldman.
newsitem.headline: Wired IPO pricing on hold - Goldman.

text.p: Wired Ventures Inc's initial public stock offering will not be priced Thursday night, as expected, according to the lead underwriter, Goldman Sachs.

No further information was immediately available, according to a spokeswoman at Goldman Sachs, who had been in contact with the firm's syndicate desk. But a further announcement may be pending, she said.
Earlier, a source close to one of the underwriters said the estimated price range had been slashed to $8 to $10 a share from the previous estimate of $12 to $14 each.

Earlier, sources familiar with the offering said the target number of shares to be sold had also been slashed to 3 million from 4.75 million as the underwriters sought to price the issue. Goldman Sachs and co-underwriter Robertson Stephens had no immediate comment on the size of the offering.

Sources in the equity investment community warned that the deal was under threat and could possibly be pulled for a second time. In July, the deal was postponed amid a broad decline in high-technology and Internet stocks.
A number of investment professionals have called the bid overpriced, even at lower levels this time around.

Wired's award-winning magazine has been regaled as the chronicle of the digital age, and it continues to report growing circulation figures. But analysts said the publication accounts for more than 90 percent of the company's revenues, with Internet-related properties making up the rest.

As such, they argue, Wired should be valued more as a publisher than as an Internet company, which have attracted soaring valuations. Furthermore, they note, the market has become more discerning on the Internet sector since its peak last spring.
